rules.name: Preparing for the Minor
rules.desc:
Students interested in German Studies should begin by taking a GERLANG 1 or GERLANG 2 language course or lower level 10 or 100-level GERMAN course as a gateway to the major.
They should consider exploring introductory literature, language, or humanities courses early to build background in literary traditions, theory, and languages.
Students should consult the department’s Program Worksheet to map out their intended course of study, electives, and potential thematic or regional focus.

rules.name: Electives
rules.desc:
• Coursework within the department. Additional GERMAN courses at the 100- or 200- level.

• Language coursework. All GERLANG courses from the Language Center may be counted.

• Bing Overseas Program. Courses taken at the Bing Overseas Studies in Berlin program with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Education as Self-Fashioning (ESF), Structured Liberal Education (SLE), relevant IntroSems or COLLEGE courses may contribute a maximum of five units.

• Coursework in other departments relevant to the degree, with approval by the Director of Undergraduate Studies.
